A has a rounder, simpler body and a calmer wood finish, while B has finer, more numerous keys and a slightly more photographic look.
B's desk has stronger wood-grain streaks and a sharper gloss, the too-textured direction the lessons penalise, while A stays smoother, like the real cards.
A's simpler, chunkier keyboard and smoother surfaces are closer to the stylised real cards than B's denser, more realistic detail.
B shows more visible grain on the desk and finer mechanical detail, while A's softer, rounder build matches the cartoonish real cards slightly better.
The two are nearly identical, but A's chunkier proportions and smoother finish lean toward the real cards' simplified toy look.
B's desk has noticeably streaky wood grain and harder highlights, which is too textured, while A keeps the smoother finish the real cards have.
